title: Jackson Pike Wastewater Treatment Plant
warnings: A NOTE HEADER MISPRINTS THE SIBLING PLANT'S PERMIT PREFIX. Part I.B.12 (sheet 20), the Downstream-Nearfield Monitoring table for station 4PF00000901, is followed by "Notes for Station Number 4PF00001001:" — that is permit prefix 4PF00001 (Columbus's OTHER plant, transcribed separately — see meta.not_in_this_corpus) with station suffix 001, not this permit's own 4PF00000901. The note's BODY text is internally consistent with THIS permit ("Sampling for the respective, common parameters shall occur on the same day as Outfall 4PF00000001"), so this reads as a copy-paste artifact in the note's label, not a real cross-reference to the sibling plant's data. Transcribed exactly as printed; not corrected, not treated as authority for anything about 4PF00001.

A SECOND NOTE HEADER IS MALFORMED, DIFFERENTLY, ON SHEET 3. The notes following the Part I.A.1 outfall-001 table are introduced "Notes for station 4PF00000001:" (sheet 3) — lowercase "station", no "Number" — where the 12 other "Notes for Station Number ..." headers in this permit (sheets 5, 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20) use the capitalized, expanded form. Transcribed exactly as printed; not corrected to match the permit's own prevailing convention. See effluent_limits_001.note_header_defect.

SHEET 19 MISSPELLS A SPECIES NAME IN A PARAMETER LABEL. The upstream (801) table's 61435 row reads "96-Hr. Acute Toxicity Pimephales promela - % Affected" — missing the terminal "s" on "promelas". The correct spelling prints two rows below, in the same table's 61441 row ("7-Day Chronic Toxicity Pimephales promelas"). Transcribed as printed at 61435, not silently normalized. See monitoring_stations.upstream_801.ambient_toxicity.acute_pimephales_promelas_96hr.

OUTFALL 001 HAS NO INITIAL/FINAL PHASE-IN — ONE TABLE COVERS THE WHOLE TERM. Unlike permits that split effluent limits into an interim and a final period, Part I.A.1 (sheets 2-4) is explicit: "During the period beginning on the effective date of this permit and lasting until the expiration date, the permittee is authorized to discharge in accordance with the following limitations..." — one table, titled "Table - Final Outfall - 001 - Final" on its face. The whole effluent toxicity parameters (61425 Ceriodaphnia dubia acute, 61426 chronic, 61427 Pimephales promelas acute, 61428 chronic) are MONITOR ONLY — no maximum, no weekly, no monthly value — for the entire permit term; no numeric WET limit is ever triggered by this permit. There is no Toxicity Reduction Evaluation schedule anywhere in Part I.C either (see schedule_of_compliance below) — a materially different toxicity posture than a permit that phases WET limits in partway through the term.

THE TSS/AMMONIA/CBOD TABLE USES A THREE-WAY SEASON SPLIT THAT DOES NOT MATCH PART III's SUMMER/WINTER DEFINITIONS. Part III, Item 1 (sheet 43) defines "Summer" as May 1 through October 31 and "Winter" as November 1 through April 30 — a two-way split, and the definition several OTHER parameters in this permit actually use (E. coli and total residual chlorine are both keyed to "Summer" alone). But the TSS (00530), ammonia (00610) and CBOD5 (80082) sub-tables in Part I.A instead print THREE distinct limit sets keyed "May", "June - Oct." and "Nov. - April" — May stands alone with its own numbers, not folded into either the general Summer or Winter period. Reading "the summer TSS limit" off this permit without checking which of the three rows is meant would silently drop the May-specific numbers. Transcribed as three separate rows below, labeled with the permit's own header text.

THE NUMERIC CHLORINE LIMIT IS PRINTED BELOW THE PERMIT'S OWN QUANTIFICATION LEVEL. Part I.A sets a Summer maximum of 0.019 mg/l for Total Residual Chlorine (50060, sheet 3). Part II, Item M (sheet 33), "Limits Below Quantification", lists exactly one parameter — Chlorine, Total Residual, PQL 0.050 mg/L — and explains that compliance with a limit set below the Ohio EPA Quantification Level is judged by the below-QL rule in OAC 3745-33-07(C), not by ordinary comparison against the raw limit value (0.019 mg/l is itself below 0.050 mg/L). Anyone auditing chlorine DMR values against the 0.019 number alone, without Item M's compliance rule, will apply the wrong test.

THIS PERMIT PRINTS NO NUMERIC BYPASS-ACTIVATION THRESHOLD FOR STATIONS 002 OR 003. Some sibling NPDES permits condition a bypass station on a hard flow precondition (e.g. "shall not divert until a sustained peak flow of N MGD is being processed through secondary treatment"). This permit's bypass tables (Part I.B.1-2, sheets 5-6, stations 4PF00000002 "at wet well" and 4PF00000003 "at headworks") carry no such language; bypass is governed only by the general provisions of Part III, Item 11 (bypass prohibited except under the 40 CFR 122.41(m) / Part III conditions) and Part II, Item F, Peak Flow Management (below), which sets a PLANT treatment-capacity figure (150 MGD wet-weather primary+secondary capacity; mass loadings at outfall 001 are based on a 68 MGD normal operating capacity) rather than a bypass-station trigger.

COORDINATES ARE GIVEN FOR THE FINAL OUTFALL AND THE CSO POINTS ONLY. Part II, Item B (sheet 24) gives a DMS coordinate for station 4PF00000001 alone among the non-CSO/non-bypass stations; bypass (002, 003), all four sludge disposal stations (581, 583, 586, 588), influent (601), upstream (801, "Frank Road bridge") and downstream (901, "Martin Marietta Aggregates bridge") are named by description only, with NO coordinate printed anywhere in this permit. The 28 CSO stations (Item D, sheets 25-28) DO each carry two coordinate pairs (relief point and discharge point). No River Mile figure appears anywhere in this document for any station — a contrast with permits (e.g. Mansfield's 2PE00001) that give an explicit River Mile on the authorization sentence.

THIS DOCUMENT DOES NOT STATE WHETHER IT IS A RENEWAL, MODIFICATION, OR NEW ISSUANCE. The only revision marker on the face of the permit is the "*QD" suffix on the permit number; nothing in the authorization sentence, Part I, Part II or Part III labels the action. `permit_action` is therefore left unset below rather than asserted from convention or from what a sibling permit's suffix has meant elsewhere in this corpus.

THE 004-052 CSO STATION RANGE IS NOT CONSECUTIVE. Part II Item B lists "4PF00000004-052" as a single range descriptor for "Combined Sewer Overflow", but Item D's station-by-station list (sheets 25-28) enumerates exactly 28 stations, not the ~49 numbers the range would imply if consecutive: 004, 005, 006, 007, 010, 011, 012, 015, 017, 018, 019, 020, 027, 028, 029, 031, 032, 033, 041, 043, 044, 045, 046, 047, 048, 049, 051, 052. Numbers like 008, 009, 013, 014, 016, 021-026, 030, 034-040, 042, 050 are simply absent from the document — not omitted here, never printed there.
MINOR: the authorization sentence's facility address prints "2104 Jackson Pike, Columbus, Ohio Franklin County" — no comma between "Ohio" and "Franklin County" — transcribed as printed (sheet 1).

fields.receiving_water_source: Named directly in the sheet-1 authorization sentence: "...to discharge from the Jackson Pike Wastewater Treatment Plant located at 2104 Jackson Pike, Columbus, Ohio Franklin County to Scioto River in accordance with the conditions specified in Parts I, II, and III of this permit." Only three Parts are named (I, II, III) — this permit has no separate stormwater/SWPPP Parts IV-VI; storm water coverage for the facility is instead handled under the separate industrial storm water general permit cited in Part II Item AC (see other_requirements_of_note.storm_water_compliance).

fields.renewal_application_due: The permit's own text requires renewal information/forms "no later than 180 days prior to the above date of expiration" — i.e. on or about 2026-07-04 for the 2026-12-31 expiration. [inference] from the permit's stated rule; the permit prints no calendar date for it. peak_flow_management.citation: Permit 4PF00000*QD, sheets 29-30, Part II Item F
peak_flow_management.text: "The Jackson Pike WWTP shall always be operated to maximize the treatment of wet weather flows from its combined sewer system. For each wet weather event, the treatment plant shall have the capacity to treat 150 MGD through the primary and secondary treatment processes." Requires a Wet Weather Operating Plan (WWOP) with procedures for treating wet-weather flow without appreciably diminishing effluent quality or destabilizing treatment on return to dry weather, and reasonable-effort staffing to maintain non-redundant critical equipment.
peak_flow_management.reporting_mechanism: "Mass loading limitations included in this permit at Outfall 4PF00000001 are based on the facility's normal operating capacity of 68 MGD. Exceedances of the mass loading limitations could occur if the volume of wet weather flow to the plant reaches a point that exceeds the normal operating capacity." During excessive/ extended wet weather, the permittee reports a MINIMUM of 68 MGD under Reporting Code 50050 (Flow Rate) and all excess flow under Reporting Code 50047 (Peak Flow Rate). Code 50047 values are NOT used in loading calculations, and may not be used when reporting under 50050 would reasonably be expected to achieve the mass loading limitation.

sso_reporting.citation: Permit 4PF00000*QD, sheets 30-32, Part II Item G
sso_reporting.prohibition: All SSOs are prohibited. An SSO does not include a listed CSO discharge.

imminent_danger_reporting.notify: Ohio EPA (1-800-282-9378) and the appropriate Board of Health within 24 hours of learning of an SSO that may imminently/substantially endanger human health.
imminent_danger_reporting.examples: dry weather overflows, major line breaks, fish kills or other significant harm, public contact with raw sewage, overflows in sensitive/high-exposure areas
imminent_danger_reporting.follow_up: Written report to the district office within 5 days, covering: estimated start/stop time, location/ID, receiving water, estimated volume, sewer component, cause, and remediation/mitigation steps with milestone schedules.

all_sso_reporting.dmr: System-wide occurrences entering waters of the state reported via station 300 (code 74062, No./Month) — see monitoring_stations.sso_300.

municipal_pretreatment_schedule.requirement: Evaluate the adequacy of local industrial user limitations to prevent pollutants entering the POTW that interfere with its operation, pass through in amounts exceeding water-quality-standard-based limits, are incompatible with the POTW, or limit wastewater/sludge use options. Submit either (a) technical justification for REVISING local limits with a pretreatment program modification request, or (b) technical justification for RETAINING existing local limits.
municipal_pretreatment_schedule.pollutants_requiring_justification: Arsenic, cadmium, total chromium, dissolved hexavalent chromium, copper, free cyanide, lead, mercury, molybdenum, nickel, selenium, silver, zinc — "unless screening of wastewater and sludge indicate these pollutants are not present in significant amounts" — plus any other pollutant needed to protect against pass through, interference or sludge disposal.
municipal_pretreatment_schedule.report_content_items: a. pollutants-of-concern identification/justification; b. plant + industrial flows to which local limits apply, including hauled-waste volumes by type; c. domestic/background concentrations (sample 3 locations x 5 consecutive days, or 2 locations x 7 consecutive days, of domestic-only wastewater); d. treatment-plant removal efficiencies (site-specific where possible); e. maximum-allowable- headworks-loading comparison across all applicable criteria; f. allocation method if revising limits; g. implementation info if narrative/BMP local limits are proposed; h. supporting data/assumptions/methodologies; i. PE stamp and signature if new/revised limits are proposed.
municipal_pretreatment_schedule.revisions: A revised report is due within 90 days of Ohio EPA notifying the permittee of deficiencies.
municipal_pretreatment_schedule.incorporation_deadline: Revised local limits must be incorporated into all industrial user control documents no later than 4 months after Ohio EPA's approval.

sampling_methods.mercury: If EPA Method 245.1 or 245.2 is used for domestic-background sampling and mercury is below detection, the permittee must use EPA Method 1631 or 245.7 to quantify domestic-background mercury.
sampling_methods.free_cyanide: ASTM D7237, OIA-1677-09, or ASTM D4282-02 (the latter requires supporting documentation that it is a "sufficiently sensitive" test procedure under 40 CFR 122.44(i)(1)(iv)).

limits_below_quantification.significance: See permit.warnings — the outfall 001 chlorine maximum (0.019 mg/l) is itself below this PQL, so compliance is judged by the below-QL arithmetic rule in OAC 3745-33-07(C), not a plain value comparison. For average limits, values below the OEPA QL are treated as zero when computing the arithmetic mean used for compliance; maximum-limit results reported below the QL are automatically in compliance.

biomonitoring_program.text: "The permittee shall continue its effluent biomonitoring program to determine the toxicity of the effluent from outfall 4PF00000001." ("Continue" implies the program predates this permit; no prior-permit text is committed in this corpus to say what triggered it.)
biomonitoring_program.testing: Annual chronic toxicity tests (Ceriodaphnia dubia and Pimephales promelas) for the life of the permit; acute endpoints derived from the chronic test; ambient/control water tested concurrently at station 4PF00000801, upstream of the effluent/ receiving-water interaction zone. Per "Reporting and Testing Guidance for Biomonitoring", Ohio EPA, July 1998 or current revision.
biomonitoring_program.sop_due: The SOP (or verification of SOP submittal) was due "no later than three months after the effective date of this permit" — on or about 2022-04-01 [inference].
biomonitoring_program.definitions: TUa = 100/LC50 (acute); TUc = 100/IC25 (chronic), or 100/sqrt(NOEC x LOEC) for Ceriodaphnia dubia where that is more restrictive, outside the mixing zone.
biomonitoring_program.note: No numeric WET limit currently attaches to this program's results — see permit.warnings on the absence of a phase-in. Ohio EPA reserves the right to modify the permit to require additional biomonitoring, a TRE, or WET limits based on the results.

pretreatment_program_requirements.text: "The permittee's pretreatment program initially approved on July 3, 1985 and all subsequent modifications approved before the effective date of this permit, shall be an enforceable term and condition of this permit."
pretreatment_program_requirements.items_summary: 1. Legal authority to implement/enforce the program, including agreements with contributing jurisdictions. 2. Sufficient resources/qualified personnel (funding). 3. Industrial-user inventory; Significant Industrial Users (SIUs) per OAC 3745-3-01 notified of standards within 30 days of determination. 4. Slug-load control-plan evaluation for each SIU at least once per control-mechanism term (existing SIUs within 1 year of the effective date if never evaluated; new SIUs within 1 year of designation). 5. Local limits, with the waste-load-allocation table below for pollutants lacking a final effluent limit. 6. Control mechanisms issued to all SIUs per OAC 3745-3-03(C)(1)(c). 7. Industrial compliance monitoring — at least annual inspection/sampling of all SIUs, 40 CFR 136 methods, repeat sampling within 30 days of a known violation (unless the IU is required to self-repeat). 8. POTW priority-pollutant monitoring — annual influent/effluent/ sludge sampling, reported on Ohio EPA Form 4221 with the annual pretreatment report. 9. Enforcement — investigate all noncompliance; publish a Significant Noncompliance (SNC) list by February 15 each year. 10. Reporting — Quarterly Industrial User Violation Report by the 15th of Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct; Annual Pretreatment Report by February 15 (program effectiveness, IU inventory, monitoring program description, pass-through/interference incidents, SNC publication copy, priority-pollutant results). 11. Records retained a minimum of 3 years (extended during unresolved litigation). 12. Program modifications — substantial changes need prior Ohio EPA approval; otherwise effective 45 days after application.

title: Southerly Wastewater Treatment Plant
warnings: A PART II CROSS-REFERENCE MISMATCH runs through station 001's own footnotes b, c and d. Notes for Station 4PF00001001 (sheet 4) read: "b. Free cyanide - See Part II, Item U.", "c. Mercury - See Part II, Item V.", and "d. Orthophosphate - See Part II, Item W." Part II's own lettering (sheets 35-36) runs U = Tracking of Group 4 Parameters (free cyanide PEL) → V = Monitoring for Free Cyanide (low-level) → W = Monitoring for Mercury (low-level) → X = Monitoring for Dissolved Orthophosphate (as P). [verified], with independent internal corroboration, that footnote c is one letter early: the influent station's own mercury footnote (Station 4PF00001601, sheet 24, footnote b) correctly cites "Item W", so the same permit cites the same item (mercury) both correctly and incorrectly in two places — that is a document self-contradiction, not a reading of ours. Footnote d (orthophosphate → printed W, titled Item X) fits the identical one-letter-early shift. [inference], not equally verified: footnote b (free cyanide → printed U) is read here as ALSO one letter early, because Item V is the item literally titled "Monitoring for Free Cyanide (low-level)" — an exact match to this row's own label (free_cyanide_low_level) — while Item U's own heading is the generic "Tracking of Group 4 Parameters." Unlike c, there is no second citation of free cyanide anywhere else in this permit to confirm b the same way 601's footnote confirms c, so reading b as wrong rests on title-matching alone, not a second internal contradiction — flagged here plainly as an interpretation, not stated as verified fact. Footnote a (chlorine → Item N) and footnote e (peak flow → Item F) and footnote f (biomonitoring → Item Z) are all unambiguously correct on both title and content. Transcribed exactly as printed in both places below; not silently corrected.

A PARAGRAPH OF PART II ITEM D REAPPEARS VERBATIM, OUT OF PLACE, INSIDE ITEM U. Part II Item D's full text — "The permittee is authorized to discharge from the following overflows only during wet weather periods when the flow in the sewer system exceeds the capacity of the sewer system. See Part III, Item 11." — is printed once correctly under heading "D." on sheet 30 (introducing the CSO overflow-location table for station 006). It is printed AGAIN, word for word, in the middle of Item U (Tracking of Group 4 Parameters) on sheet 35, wedged between the free-cyanide PEL reduction requirement and the heading for Item V, with no heading letter of its own and no connection to the surrounding free-cyanide text. Confirmed against a layout-mode re-extraction of sheet 35 (identical result), so this is the document's own duplication defect, not a pypdf extraction artifact. Transcribed as printed at both locations; the sheet-35 occurrence is not treated as a second, independent Item D.

THE FACT SHEET'S TWO FIGURE CAPTIONS ARE BROKEN CROSS-REFERENCES, and the figures' content is a coverage gap. Sheet "Page 3 of 6" of the Fact Sheet reads "...Error! Reference source not found. shows the approximate location of the facility" and "...which are shown on Error! Reference source not found.:" — an unresolved Microsoft Word cross-reference field, left in the document as exported to PDF, at both points where the Fact Sheet means to name the two figures that follow it (Figure 1, a topographic location map, and Figure 2, a process-flow diagram — see permit.embedded_images). The figures themselves carry real content — station labels and the plant's full process train — that exists ONLY in the image and nowhere in the extractable text of this PDF. See permit.embedded_images for what was established about them by direct inspection.

THE FACILITY'S OWN MAILING ADDRESS IS GIVEN TWO DIFFERENT WAYS in this same PDF for the same street address, and the document itself resolves why. The cover letter (PDF page 0) addresses the permittee at "6977 South High Street, Columbus, OH 43206". The issued permit itself (sheet 1) and the Fact Sheet (Page 1 of 6) both give the facility's location as "6977 South High Street, Lockbourne, Ohio" / "Lockbourne, OH 43137", Franklin County. But the Fact Sheet's own "Name and Address of Applicant" block (Page 1 of 6) gives the applicant's mailing address as "1250 Fairwood Avenue, Columbus, OH 43206" — the identical ZIP the cover letter used. So the cover letter is not carrying Lockbourne mail under a different ZIP; it pairs the plant's own street address (6977 South High Street) with the applicant's own corporate mailing ZIP (43206, the same ZIP printed at 1250 Fairwood Avenue), not the facility's Lockbourne ZIP (43137). Both are transcribed below at their respective fields.

THE SCHEDULE OF COMPLIANCE IS RETIRED, NOT ACTIVE, in this permit — the opposite of Mansfield's 2PE00001*PD, which carries a live, dated Toxicity Reduction Evaluation schedule. Part I,C here (sheet 27) lists exactly two items, both parenthetically marked "(COMPLETE)", with NO due dates and NO event codes: "A. Municipal Pretreatment Schedule (COMPLETE)" and "B. Chemically-Enhanced Primary Treatment Effectiveness Study (COMPLETE)". The cover letter and Fact Sheet explain why: "the permittee has completed all schedule of compliance requirements in the current permit; Part I,C is proposed to be modified accordingly." So this modification's own express purpose was to close out the schedule that used to be here (under the prior *RD permit, not committed in this corpus) — there is no compliance clock running on this facility as of this permit.

SHEET 5 PRINTS STATION 090'S OWN NUMBER TWO WAYS, AND CARRIES A RUN-TOGETHER WORD; SHEET 29 LEAVES A PARENTHESIS UNCLOSED. Sheet 5's notes block header reads "Notes for Station Number 4PF0000190:" — nine digits, missing the "1" that makes the station's real number 4PF00001090 (ten digits, as printed everywhere else in this document, including the table heading two lines above on the same sheet: "outfall: 4PF00001090"). The same sheet's footnote a reads "...on each day when the CEPT system is inoperation and wastewater is being discharged..." — "is inoperation" printed as one run-together word. Separately, on sheet 29, the Item B location table's row for 4PF00001090 reads: '"Fictitious station" - final effluent, prior to discharge to Scioto River, includes effluents from secondary treatment and CEPT (report at this station when CEPT is operating' — the opening parenthesis is never closed before the row ends. All three are the document's own printing defects, transcribed as printed; none is corrected here.

Only THREE of the five — 581, 583 and 584 — carry the 9-metal ceiling table and the nutrient (ammonia/TKN/TP/potassium) panel; 586 and 588 carry neither, weight only — see the comparison below. Only 584 additionally carries a Pollutant Concentration (monthly-average) limit set and a Salmonella limit.

influent_601.description: "Influent Monitoring" (sheet 23 heading) — printed with no further location detail (no "downstream of..." or similar qualifier); unlike Mansfield's 2PE00001*ND-successor, this permit does not say "bar screen" or any other reference point here.
influent_601.parameters: TSS, total cyanide, nickel, zinc, cadmium, lead, total chromium, copper, dissolved hexavalent chromium, low-level mercury, pH (max and min), CBOD 5-day — all monitor-only.
influent_601.note: Footnote a: "Sampling for the respective/common parameters shall occur on the same day as Outfall 4PF00001001." Footnote b: "Mercury - See Part II, Item W." — this one CORRECTLY cites Item W (mercury); contrast with station 001's footnote c, which cites the same item as "V" — see warnings[0].

upstream_801.description: Receiving stream, upstream of the point of discharge
upstream_801.chemistry: pH, ammonia, TKN, nitrite+nitrate, total phosphorus — 1/Month Grab, all months
upstream_801.ambient_toxicity: 48-hr acute and 7-day chronic Ceriodaphnia dubia, 96-hr acute and 7-day chronic Pimephales promelas — all "1/Year Grab, May", reported as "% Affected", no limits.
upstream_801.note: Footnote a: same-day-as-001 sampling. Footnote b: "Biomonitoring - See Part II, Item Z."

downstream_nearfield_901.description: Receiving stream, downstream of the point of discharge, at the State Route 762 bridge
downstream_nearfield_901.parameters: Water temperature, pH, ammonia, TKN, nitrite+nitrate, total phosphorus, total hardness (as CaCO3) — 1/Month Grab, all months; E. coli 1/2 Weeks Grab, June-Aug.
downstream_nearfield_901.note: Footnote a: same-day-as-001 sampling, identical wording to 801.

schedule_of_compliance.note: No milestones, no dates, no event codes anywhere in this Part — both items are printed as already satisfied. See warnings[4] for what this modification did to get here.

peak_flow_operations.text: "The Southerly WWTP shall always be operated to maximize the treatment of wet weather flows from its combined sewer system. For each wet weather event, the treatment plant shall have the capacity to treat 330 MGD through the primary and secondary treatment processes." Mass-loading limits at 001 are based on 114 MGD normal operating capacity; during excess wet-weather flow the permittee may report flow above 114 MGD under Reporting Code 50047 (Peak Flow Rate) rather than 50050 (Flow Rate), and 50047 values are excluded from loading calculations.

cept_bypass_authority.text: "A CSO-related bypass of the secondary treatment portion... of the POTW treatment plant is approved when the influent flow rate to the facility exceeds 330 MGD. ...At a minimum, CSO-related bypass flows must receive solids and floatables removal, primary clarification, and disinfection... provided by the Chemically Enhanced Primary Treatment (CEPT) system." Notice of any CEPT-related bypass is due to Ohio EPA within 24 hours.

percent_removal_requirement.text: "The treatment works must obtain at least 85 percent removal of carbonaceous biochemical oxygen demand (five-day) and suspended solids (see Part III, Item 1)." The only percent-removal limit in this permit — distinct from the concentration/load limits at 001 (effluent_limits_001) and from the sampling-timing use of "percent removal" in station 601's own text (Part I,B.9, sheet 23: "Samples of influent used for determination of net values or percent removal must be taken the same day as those samples of effluent used for that determination").

limits_below_quantification.note: The one PQL entry in this permit — matches footnote a on station 001's chlorine limit (0.020 mg/l maximum, below this 0.050 mg/L PQL).

pretreatment_local_limits_wla.note: Waste load allocation values the permittee must use "when evaluating local limits... for which a final effluent limit has not been established" — a SEPARATE dataset from the Group 4 free-cyanide PEL (16/60 ug/L, see below) and from the plant's own Part I.A limits, which carry no numeric metals limits at all.

pretreatment_program.approved: July 3, 1985, and all subsequent modifications approved before the effective date
pretreatment_program.note: Indexed, not transcribed in full: legal authority, funding, industrial user inventory (30-day notification of Significant Industrial User status), slug load control plans, local limits (see table above), control mechanisms, industrial compliance monitoring, annual POTW priority-pollutant monitoring, enforcement (SNC publication by Feb 15), quarterly/annual reporting, 3-year record retention, program modifications (45-day default effective date for non-substantial changes).

group_4_tracking.trigger: Written notification to Ohio EPA Central District Office within 30 days if the max PEL is exceeded 4+ months in any consecutive 6-month period, OR the avg PEL is exceeded 2+ months in any consecutive 6-month period; reduction below PEL required within 6 months of either trigger (or a compliance-schedule modification request).

biomonitoring_program.text: "The permittee shall continue to implement an effluent biomonitoring program to determine the toxicity of the effluent from outfall 4PF00001001."
biomonitoring_program.testing: Annual chronic (Ceriodaphnia dubia + Pimephales promelas) and acute bioassays per the July 1998 Ohio EPA biomonitoring guidance; ambient/control water from upstream station 801. SOP or verification of SOP submittal due within 3 months of the effective date (2026-01-01 [inference] — three calendar months after the 2025-10-01 effective date).
biomonitoring_program.definitions: TUa = 100/LC50. TUc = 100/IC25, or 100/sqrt(NOEC x LOEC) for Ceriodaphnia dubia where that is more restrictive.

outfall_signage.note: Standard sign requirements at every regulated outfall/bypass/CSO; SSO signage specifically grandfathered under "SSO Consent Order (Case No. 02-CVH-05-5768; entered August 1, 2002)" — matches the same case number in the Fact Sheet's consent-order recital (see permit.fact_sheet.consent_orders).

storm_water_general_permit.text: Coverage under industrial storm water general permit 4GR00607*EG, effective September 13, 2017; renewal request due within 90 days of the general permit's next renewal.

facility_description.population_served: approximately 1.3 million (City of Columbus and many other municipalities)
facility_description.treatment_processes: Bar and Fine Screening, Grit Removal, Primary Clarification, Activated Sludge, Secondary Clarification, Chlorination/Dechlorination, Post-Aeration

consent_orders.integrated_plan: "The Integrated Plan and Wet Weather Management Plan Update Report" submitted 2015-09-15, approved by Ohio EPA 2015-12-01.

fact_sheet.cept_history: Completed December 2019. "The CEPT is an authorized CSO-related bypass which provides primary clarification and chlorine disinfection to an additional 110 MGD." Blended with secondary effluent prior to station 001. "Influent flows that exceed the combined capacity of secondary treatment and the CEPT (440 MGD) are discharged via outfall 002, a raw sewage bypass located at the facility headworks."
fact_sheet.cso_ownership_split: "The collection system tributary to Southerly WWTP has 94% separated sewers and 6% combined sewers. There are 31 CSOs in the Columbus collection system. Only CSO 006 is authorized in the Southerly NPDES permit, the other 30 are authorized in the NPDES permit for Jackson Pike WWTP (4PF00000)." This is the document's own statement of the two-permit CSO split; the other 30 CSOs and Jackson Pike's own figures are NOT transcribed here — that is the other agent's document, per this task's instructions.
